My land is about 5 mu here in Quzhou. I have farmed it since I was young. My sons are in the city now — Shijiazhuang — so I mostly do it myself, maybe with a neighbor's help at harvest. I do not read, but I know this soil. I know the seasons.

I will grow what I always grow: wheat in the winter, corn in the summer. Everyone here does this. The grain station buys it, the price is stable enough, and I know exactly what to do. I am not going to try something new at my age on land I depend on.

For the wheat, I will plant in mid-October after I hire the rotary tiller. I will buy the Ji-mai variety from the village supply co-op — same as last year, it did fine. I will put down the compound fertilizer before planting, then spread urea in March when the wheat starts to stand up again. I will water it before the ground freezes, then again in spring at jointing. Maybe once more at grain-filling if the well has water. I will spray herbicide once and check for rust — if I see orange spots I will spray again.

After I sell the wheat in June, I will plant corn right away, no tilling — my neighbor stopped tilling for summer corn years ago and it saves my back. I will use Zhengdan 958 — everyone uses it, it is reliable. I will put fertilizer in the furrow and topdress again when it is knee high. Summer rains usually come, but I will pump from the well once at silking if it is dry. I will watch for the worm that came a few years ago and spray if I see damage.
